title: bug: every fresh publish reads UNKNOWN, and is offered the operator's Resolve, while its one push is still in flight
description:
Found by worker-952c612b during task-21be6e9055984413a651ce6ee331e2c8's adversarial review. Evidence is code only: no probe was run.

WHY THE WINDOW EXISTS. node-publisher.ts:186-189 journals the intent BEFORE its one push (:202). run-goal-publication.ts:13 calls any intent with no receipt UNKNOWN. affordance-read answers `unknownPublishDecision` from that same read, so affordance-planning-offers.ts:255 mints repository.publish_resolve. Result: for the seconds between the intent commit and the post-push receipt, the Publish card shows UNKNOWN and the Resolve buttons.

WHAT A CLICK IN THAT WINDOW DOES.
1. The operator's NOT_TRANSMITTED or ABANDON records the REFUSED receipt first. recordPublishReceipt keeps the first writer: publish-ledger.ts:203-204.
2. If the push lands, the publisher's PUSHED write gets that REFUSED receipt back. It reports UNKNOWN "remote holds the sha but the recorded receipt does not match the candidate" (:217-219).
3. On the next pass it gives the hold back as PUBLISH_RESOLVED.
4. The card then says REFUSED while the remote holds the commit.
The cost is bounded: a later decision's push of the same sha is a git no-op, and a remote that has moved on is refused PUBLISH_REMOTE_DIVERGED by the pre-flight. So the effect is not transmitted twice, but the record is wrong.

HINT FOR THE FIX, left to the architect. A live controller does NOT tell in-flight from stuck: a stuck publish's hold is also owned by the live wrapper. The fix must also keep a publish that was stuck before task-78dea88b resolvable; such a publish has no transmission record. publish-resolve-journey.test.ts's step (4) pins the card at UNKNOWN for a stuck publish.
definitionOfDone: While a fresh publish's single push is in flight (intent journaled, no receipt), the card does not say UNKNOWN and the affordance read offers no repository.publish_resolve. A test pins this against the production read and the production offer mint.
A stuck UNKNOWN publish is still offered the resolve. This includes one stuck before task-78dea88b, which has no transmission record. publish-resolve-journey.test.ts stays green.

implementationPlan.description:
RED, in apps/daemon/src/http/affordance-read-planning.test.ts, the describe "and the publish resolve card on the same landed goal" (:1529 onward). It already drives the production offer mint through the shipped composition root and reads the card with the production read.

EVERY ARM INJECTS ITS CLOCK. That means the affordance read's config.clock, plus the same instant passed to `card(store, now)`, since the card helper must mirror runs-read. Nothing may depend on the wall clock. The fixture's AT is 2026-09-19T08:00Z, so an arm that read the wall clock would change its answer at about 08:0x UTC: a date-dependent flake.

The arms. B is the bound named in step 3.
- IN FLIGHT: an intent at AT, no receipt, no observation, now = AT + 1 s. The card reads `outcome: "PENDING", code: null`, and the offers carry NO `repository.publish_resolve` (DoD 1).
- STUCK BY AGE: the same records, now = AT + B. The card reads UNKNOWN / PUBLISH_EFFECT_RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED, and the resolve is offered on `publish-resolve:<decisionId>`.
- JUST INSIDE: now = AT + B - 1 ms is still in flight. This pins which side of the boundary the bound sits on.
- STUCK BY OBSERVATION: intent plus `notePublicationObservation(...)`, now = AT + 1 s. UNKNOWN plus the offer, IMMEDIATELY: the pass finished and could not settle it.
- LEGACY STUCK (DoD 2): an intent from before task-78dea88b, with no transmission record and no observation, now = AT + B. UNKNOWN plus the offer.

The existing arms in this describe that expect UNKNOWN from an intent alone must now inject now >= AT + B, or add an observation. Re-pin them by the rule; never widen a matcher.

Run the file and CONFIRM the in-flight and just-inside arms are RED, quoting them.

implementationPlan.description:
GREEN.

(1) apps/daemon/src/repository/git-publication-port.ts: export `PUBLICATION_GIT_TIMEOUT_MS = 60_000` and use it at :20 in place of the literal. No behaviour change.

(2) apps/daemon/src/http/run-goal-publication.ts:
- Add an optional fourth parameter `now?: number` (epoch ms).
- Export `PUBLISH_IN_FLIGHT_BOUND_MS`, derived as (git calls on the longest path, from step 1(a)) × PUBLICATION_GIT_TIMEOUT_MS + one PUBLICATION_GIT_TIMEOUT_MS of margin. Put the derivation in a comment citing the node-publisher.ts sites. At planning that is 6 minutes.
- In the pending loop, a request whose intent exists without a receipt is IN FLIGHT iff ALL of these hold: `now` was passed; readPublicationObservation(...) is null; `Date.parse(intent.intendedAt)` is finite; and `now - intendedAt < PUBLISH_IN_FLIGHT_BOUND_MS`.
- An in-flight request is selected as the request, but it is NOT unknown. It reads PENDING with code null, and the card keeps its exact key set.
- Everything else keeps today's UNKNOWN. That includes: an observation read that throws; an intent read that throws (already UNKNOWN); an unparseable intendedAt; and every caller that passes no `now`. Each of these fails TOWARD the operator's exit, because a stuck publish must never be hidden.
- Keep the file small: 27 lines at planning.

(3) apps/daemon/src/http/runs-read.ts goalView (:271): pass `Date.parse(now)`, using the runs read's own injectable clock (:211, :299). This is the Publish card's production read.

(4) apps/daemon/src/http/affordance-read.ts :405-407: pass `Date.parse(now)` from the same read's clock (:355), so the offer and the card judge the SAME instant. Update the comment above it: the resolve is offered while the card says UNKNOWN, which is never during the publish's own in-flight window.

Confirm every arm from step 2 is GREEN.

comments.author: qa-6e60f228
comments.content:
QA follow-ups (qa-6e60f228, reviewed 779f540b). These are not rows, per DELIVERY BIAS. None blocks: the delivered bytes behave correctly.

1. The runs-read wiring is UNPINNED. runs-read.ts:271 passes Date.parse(now), and that is the Publish card's served read. I ran an in-memory mutant (out-of-tree vitest transform, enforce:pre, anchor-throw, QA_DRILL_APPLIED=1) that dropped that argument. affordance-read-planning.test.ts plus runs-read.test.ts stayed 76/76 GREEN. The card() helper calls readRunGoalPublication directly with its own now, so it cannot see this wiring. The afford mutant (drop Date.parse(now) at affordance-read.ts:407) and the pre-fix mutant (intent => UNKNOWN) both go RED on IN FLIGHT and JUST INSIDE, so the offer half is pinned. To pin the card half, readRuns needs a goal it can serve. The seed world here does not work: readRuns({goalRef: SEED_GOAL}) refuses RUNS_READ_GOAL_UNKNOWN because the goal is not catalog-bound. Use the bound-goal world from control-room live-runs.test.ts DAEMON_RUNS_SOURCE instead (bootstrap-test-fixtures driveThrough goal.create, then goal.create_with_source). My probe on that world (cwd apps/daemon, node --experimental-strip-types) wrote an intent at 08:00Z with no observation and read createRunsReadPort({clock}).readRuns({goalRef}) at several clocks:
- +1s: PENDING/null
- B-1ms: PENDING/null
- B: UNKNOWN/PUBLISH_EFFECT_RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED
- 'not-a-time': UNKNOWN
- the wall clock (45 min later): UNKNOWN

2. A NEGATIVE AGE reads PENDING. If the read clock is behind intendedAt, for example after a backward step of the host clock, then now - intendedAt < B holds. The same probe with the read clock 1 h before intendedAt gave PENDING/null. A stuck publish is then hidden for the skew plus 5 min. Treating every negative age as UNKNOWN is wrong, because of the ms race between the read's clock() and a concurrent intent commit. A clamp such as `age < -B => UNKNOWN` would bound it.

3. The bound VALUE is not pinned. Every arm is relative to the exported B, so changing the multiplier from 4 to 40 stays green; only a non-finite B would red it. The bound counts 4 network port calls (observe, push, ls-remote --symref, observe). The roughly 9 local execFile calls on that path (init --bare x4, rev-parse, cat-file, config --get-urlmatch x3) share the 1x margin. Each of those also has a 60 s timeout, so this is realistic but not the execFile-level worst case.

4. affordance-read.ts was 669 lines at the parent and is 670 here (+1 comment line). It was already over the 400 cap, so this is NOT charged to this row. Whoever owns splitting affordance-read.ts should take it.

5. The worker's comment-80a5e9b5 follow-ups stand: the resolve service still accepts a crafted in-flight dispatch, and goal-deployment-read and release-evidence-read call without now.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
1. UNKNOWN only once an observation exists, with no clock. Rejected: several post-intent UNKNOWN exits write NO observation, for example a remote that stays unreadable (node-publisher.ts:204), a refused transition, or an intent that approves a different candidate. Such a stuck publish would read PENDING forever and never get its resolve, which violates DoD 2.
2. Use the transmission record as the push-done signal. Rejected: a publish that got stuck before task-78dea88b has none (the row's own warning), and the window extends past the push anyway, through observe and the receipt.
3. Use liveness of the reservation holder. Rejected: the row's hint notes that a stuck publish's hold is also owned by the live wrapper.
4. CHOSEN: an age bound DERIVED from the git timeouts on the longest in-flight path, plus an observation short-circuit. It needs no new record and no wire change. PENDING already exists in the card's vocabulary, and the fix is scoped to the two reads the card and the offer use.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
Measured 2026-09-19 by architect-c7fb990e at HEAD 03fae5b3.
- run-goal-publication.ts is 27 lines: an intent without a receipt is UNKNOWN (:11-16), and otherwise the outcome is the receipt's or PENDING (:24).
- affordance-read.ts:405-407 offers the resolve iff the card read says UNKNOWN. Its clock is at :355, from config.clock or the wall clock.
- runs-read.ts:271 is the card's publish read, and its injectable clock is at :211/:299 (goalView receives `now`).
- node-publisher.ts writes, in order: the intent (:186); in transmit, observe (:87), push (:91) and the transmission record (:95); then observe (:203); then notLanded's observe and contains (:137-139); then the receipt or the observation. That is at most 5 git calls, each with a 60 s timeout (git-publication-port.ts:20).
- The observation record carries decisionId, expectedSha, observedAt, observedSha and reason (publication-effect-ledger.ts:120), and is written only on the not-landed path.
- runs-read.test.ts has no publish arm. The production-path arms live in affordance-read-planning.test.ts :1523 onward.
planningNotes.risks:
1. DATE FLAKES: fixtures use fixed timestamps such as AT 2026-09-19T08:00Z. Any arm that lets the read use the wall clock flips at a real date. Every arm injects its clock, and callers without `now` keep today's semantics.
2. A stuck publish that nothing observed reads PENDING for up to the bound (about 6 min) before its resolve appears. That is the accepted cost; an observed stuck publish is immediate.
3. The bound is only as good as its derivation. If step 1 counts a different number of git calls, the constant follows the measurement and not the planning number.
4. The service does not re-check in-flight, so a crafted dispatch can still resolve in the window. That is a follow-up for defence in depth; the UI can no longer offer it.
